properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 26 at 10:09AM AST until October 26 at 5:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Portions of Puerto Rico and Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.headline: Sedgwick County testing outdoor warning devices
properties.description: Sedgwick County Emergency Management will be testing the Outdoor Warning Sirens at Noon Today. Sedgwick County outdoor warning sirens are tested every Monday at Noon except Holidays and when threatening weather is present. Today we will be testing the Alert mode for one minute. The Alert Mode is a steady tone used for Tornado warning The Attack Mode is a classic rise and fall sound used for Air Attack Warning in times of war. Outdoor warning sirens are designed to be an early warning device primarily for persons who are outside away from the television and or radio. Remember when the outdoor warning sirens sound Take cover Tune in to local media Take action.
properties.instruction: Emergency Management officials highly recommend citizens keep a NOAA weather radio in their homes preferably in the bedroom with a tone alert for those times when you are not monitoring public media. This broadcast originates from Sedgwick County Emergency Management located at seven fourteen North Main Wichita Kansas. WPMQ three ninety one. No action required test only.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 9:55AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds are causing river levels to rise on
the St Johns at Astor, currently in Moderate Flood Stage. The river
is forecast to continue to climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage
early this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EDT Monday the stage was 3.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EDT Monday was 3.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.8 feet
this evening.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1130 PM EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Navajo, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 6:10AM MST until October 26 at 9:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the Little Colorado River from earlier
excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Birdsprings to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until 900 AM MST /1000 AM MDT/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring near
Birdsprings. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 605 AM MST /705 AM MDT/, water levels overnight have continued
to fall along the Little Colorado River at Winslow. As flow
continues to decrease through the morning, the threat for
flooding will diminish at Birdsprings by mid-morning.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 6:00am MST /7:00am MDT/ the stage was 14.89 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Water levels are forecast to continue to fall through
the day.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of rivers are unstable and
unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous. Do not attempt to cross
flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 AM MST /10 AM MDT/ THIS MORNING

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 26 at 3:05AM HST until October 29 at 5:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
A trough moving over the state should bring abundant tropical
moisture and is expected to remain nearly stationary for a few days.
Heavy rain and isolated thunderstorms are possible, potentially
leading to flooding across all islands.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...All main Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Flood prone roads and other low lying areas may be closed
due to elevated runoff and overflowing streams. Urban areas may
receive more significant flooding and property damage due to rapid
runoff.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms with intense rain rates
may develop Tuesday and continue through Wednesday evening as a
trough moves over the state.
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.description:

into the weekend. Winds and seas will increase Friday afternoon ahead
of the approaching typhoon, potentially exceeding hazardous levels
to small craft by late Friday night, with seas approaching 10 feet.
Mariners are urged to remain weather aware over the coming days.

properties.areaDesc: Tinian Coastal Waters; Saipan Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 26 at 10:15PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Typhoon In-fa will approach the far northern CNMI late Friday and
into the weekend. Winds and seas will sharply increase starting early
Friday ahead of the approaching typhoon, quickly exceeding hazardous
levels to small craft early on Friday. Seas of 10 to 15 feet are
expected to develop in the coastal of Tinian and Saipan. Although,
sustained winds are not expected to reach tropical-storm force at
this time, tropical-storm force gusts are possible. Mariners are
urged to remain weather aware over the coming days.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 6:54AM CDT until October 26 at 10:00AM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Southeastern Dallam County in the panhandle of Texas...
Northeastern Hartley County in the panhandle of Texas...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Low-water crossings are inundated
with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 654 AM CDT, local law enforcement reported flooding in the
warned area. Flooding is already occurring. Between 3 and 4
inches of rain have fallen.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Dalhart and Hartley.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.areaDesc: Guadalupe, NM
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 26 at 5:25AM MDT until October 26 at 8:30AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...East Central Guadalupe County in east central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 830 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos. Dangerous flows
over low-water crossings. Water over roadways. Overflowing poor
drainage areas. Some low-water crossings may become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 521 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause arroyo and small stream flooding.
Up to 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Hazardous water levels will impact Alamagordo Creek, Arroyo
Copita, and Arroyo Potrillo, downstream to the Pecos River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of East Central Guadalupe County.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 830 AM MDT THIS MORNING

properties.description:

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and

* WHEN...Until 6 PM CDT this evening.

direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the

properties.areaDesc: Culebra
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 26 at 6:14AM AST until October 27 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...Beaches along the west to northeast coasts of Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip

shorelines and tidal waterways.

deeper water.

morning high tide will be the highest of the two daily tides.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

water. Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer or surfer head
first into the bottom causing neck and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels will continue to rise with a
King Tide Cycle in place through the upcoming work-week. The
morning high tide will be the highest of the two daily tides.
King Tides peak Tuesday and Wednesday.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Shore break occurs when waves break directly on the beach. It is
extremely important to protect your head and neck whenever you
are in breaking waves by keeping your hands in front of you at
all times.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Colleton; Charleston
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 26 at 2:35AM EDT until October 26 at 11:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 1
to 4 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, one to
two feet of inundation above ground level expected along
shorelines and tidal waterways (7.9 to 8.1 feet Mean Lower Low
Water at Charleston).

* WHERE...Coastal Colleton and Charleston Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 2 PM EDT this
afternoon. For the High Rip Current Risk, through this
evening. For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 11 AM EDT this
morning.

* IMPACTS...Significant saltwater inundation will render
numerous roads impassable. Properties may also flood.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide will occur around 8:18 AM today
at Charleston. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2
hours before and after high tide.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Visit water.weather.gov for additional water level and flood
impact information.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 26 at 1:39AM EDT until October 29 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
7 to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 AM EDT Thursday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Significant shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 8:19PM AKDT until October 28 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding, with water levels of 1 to 2.5 feet
above the normal highest tide line, and 30 to 40 mph southwest
winds with gusts up to 40 to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM AKDT Wednesday, highest water levels expected
during each upcoming high tide through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Steady south to southwesterly flow is
expected to continue for the Kuskokwim Delta coastline through
Wednesday morning as a series of low pressure systems track
across the Bering Sea. Coastal erosion and minor coastal
flooding will be possible with each upcoming high tide due to
the persistent onshore winds, during which maximum water levels
will reach between 1 and 2.5 ft above the normal highest tide
line, including in and around Kipnuk and Kwigillingok. The
strong winds may reduce the ability for flood waters to recede
during and close to low tide, possibly leading to prolonged
higher than normal water levels along the coast and near the
mouth of the Kuskokwim River. There will be a break in strong
winds between Wednesday afternoon and Thursday morning,
however, we are monitoring the potential for another strong
storm system that could cause additional coastal impacts towards
the end of this week.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 AM AKDT WEDNESDAY

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 8:36PM PDT until October 29 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...From 9 AM Monday to 3 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at
11:39 AM Monday 10/26, 1.8 ft above normal (7.6 ft MLLW) at
12:15 PM Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at
12:56 PM Wednesday 10/28, and 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft
MLLW) at 01:43 PM Thursday 10/29. These predictions include up
to 1.0 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 7:44PM MDT until October 29 at 8:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...Until Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, streets in the village of San Francisco
between interstate 25 and the Rio Grande just south of Bernardo are
being flooded. Water levels in the Lower Rio Puerco have not been
this high since July of 1944. The nearby railroad bridge may also
be flooded. Further rises will impact Interstate 25 traffic.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:00 PM MDT Sunday the stage was 20.0 feet. No reliable
observations available thereafter.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum known river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 3:00 PM MDT Sunday was 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 24.2 feet
just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
early Thursday morning.
- Flood stage is 19.5 feet.
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Monday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Sunday to 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be Monday
through Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated
Coastal Flood Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger
surf develops.
properties.instruction:

NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Hawaii in Hawaii, HI; Oahu in Honolulu, HI; Kauai, HI; Maui, HI
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 25 at 3:08PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
ESFHFO

A significant pattern change is expected late Monday night through at
least Thursday as deep tropical moisture is brought north. A
combination of surface lows and troughs will bring exceptionally
moist air over the state beginning late Monday night. Heavy rain and
isolated thunderstorms are possible throughout this period. Models
have not converged on details yet, so exact locations, timing, and
rainfall amounts are not certain. Please be prepared for periods of
heavy rain this coming week.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through the
Internet (weather.gov/hawaii), local media, social media, or NOAA
Weather Radio broadcasts.

An updated outlook will be issued MOnday by 6 AM HST or sooner if
necessary.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 2:29PM MDT until October 26 at 3:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northwestern Valencia County in central New Mexico...
Northeastern Cibola County in west central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 330 PM MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 226 PM MDT, emergency management reported continued flooding
through the Rio San Jose basin, which is still out of banks in
large stretches. Any additional rainfall this afternoon will
exacerbate ongoing flooding.
- Flooding will continue along the Rio San Jose.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Grants, Laguna Pueblo, New Laguna, Cubero, Mesita, San Fidel,
Skyline-Ganipa, McCartys, Paraje and Seama.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

properties.areaDesc: Hawaii in Hawaii, HI; Oahu in Honolulu, HI; Kauai, HI; Maui, HI
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 25 at 4:13AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
ESFHFO

A significant pattern change is expected Monday night through at
least Thursday as deep tropical moisture is brought north. A
combination of surface lows and troughs will bring exceptionally
moist air over the eastern end of the state beginning Monday night
and extending to all islands Tuesday. Heavy rain and thunderstorms
are possible throughout this period. Models have not converged on
details yet, so exact locations, timing, and rainfall amounts are not
certain. Please be prepared for periods of heavy rain this coming
week.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through the
Internet (weather.gov/hawaii), local media, social media, or NOAA
Weather Radio broadcasts.

An updated outlook will be issued Sunday by 6 PM HST or sooner if
necessary.
